claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child. Their name is Alex and they're 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 19 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility, as Child Benefit rules are different for children over 16.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, NVQs, or a traineeship)? This would need to be full-time and non-advanced education (not university level).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. They're studying for their A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know, thank you.

Since Alex is 19 and studying A-levels, I have a couple more questions:

When did Alex turn 19? (I ask because there are specific rules about the cut-off age for Child Benefit when a child is in approved education.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex turned 19 back in February, so a few months ago now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

I need to check one more detail about Alex's education. Do you know when Alex started their current A-level course, and when is it expected to finish? Also, did Alex register or enroll on this course before they turned 19?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex started the A-levels in September last year, so they were still 18 then. The course is a two-year program, so it should finish next summer - around June or July next year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me also check the specific rules about Child Benefit when a child turns 16:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I just have a couple more questions to confirm eligibility:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you?
3. Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me. No, Alex isn't working - they're focused on their studies. And they don't get any benefits themselves.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming those details.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex lives with you, so you are responsible for them
- ✅ Although Alex is 19, they are under 20 and in approved education (A-levels count as approved, non-advanced education)
- ✅ Alex is not working 24 hours or more per week
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in their own right

You can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex until they either finish their A-level course (expected next summer) or turn 20, whichever comes first.

If you haven't already, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
